authorization: Standing autonomous modelling approval; every new end-use/technology screening convention remains explicit for later review.
limitations: This cohort reviews exact native boiler/stove and industrial-heating inputs. Other turbine/CHP, biomethane, mobile machinery, waste-gas and direct-process/foreground emissions still require review. No complete public emissions support is implied.

Preserve every complete native burner at its original+1MJfuel-input reference; caller heat outputs may have different reference quantities and efficiencies. No extra thermal-efficiency, 3.6MJ/kWh, concentration, allocation or heat-recovery factor is introduced.

Dedicated1MWnatural-gas furnaces and asphalt process furnaces use the corresponding industrial fuel role. Above100kWgenericgasboilers use industrial gas as a documented screening convention. For smallgas/oil/LPGboilers, heat-producing wrapper records use residential-heating roles; direct production/disposal-site thermal inputs use the corresponding industrial fuel role as an explicit use-sector proxy. This does not establish the actual factory space/process-heat split, fleet composition or industrial-scale equipment.

Automatic15/50kWpellet and50kWchip heating uses the modern residential-biomass role; log-heating/stoves use residential traditional biomass heat, not cooking; coal stoves use residential coal heat. Direct manufacturing uses and300kWwood furnaces use industrial fuel roles. End-use shares, institutional/service boundaries, source technology/vintage/geography and unquantified score effects remain uncertain; source inventories are not upgraded or replaced.

The separately inspected300kWwoodinventory without fuel input has a valid+1MJreference, distinct1990sair/ash/electricity coefficients, and zero fuel/freight entries. Apply only its own reviewed gaseous-air reductions, retaining its zero upstream fuel/freight and every native baseline difference. Do not copy the ordinary furnace, add fuel burdens, reinterpret by-product allocation or add credits. Nine earlier retained pairs are explicitly superseded by this independent source review.

Only reviewed gaseous air reductions change. Non-air releases, CO2, particles, aggregate VOC, upstream fuels/infrastructure and all signed caller quantities/formulas/uncertainty are retained. Special project variants are outside this cohort and are not silently treated as interchangeable inventory versions.

Exact native construction-machine fuel combustion uses the GAINS non-road diesel or gasoline role. This does not establish road-vehicle, agricultural-tractor, shipping or power-generation equivalence, nor a physical machinery/fleet upgrade.

Preserve each complete native +1MJ fuel-reference inventory, signed caller quantities, formulas, uncertainty, fuel demand, infrastructure, lubricant and disposal boundaries. Fuel-only variants stay fuel-only; missing infrastructure or lubricants are not added. Multiple same-supplier entries stay separate and each retains its own literal audit.

Petrol source includes copied diesel wording, but its inspected positive fuel input is Petrol, at regional storage. Preserve the actual petrol inventory rather than copying diesel coefficients or correcting documentation through invented quantities.

Native particle-filter/average fleet distinctions and all PM, CO2, non-air, aggregate VOC and unreviewed species remain unchanged. Apply only reviewed gaseous air reductions with the existing reduction-only convention; no new filter efficiency or speciation is inferred.

Global filtered-diesel source uses an older Swiss off-road baseline and warns against high relative importance. Preserve its complete historical baseline, global label and World GAINS lookup, with unquantified technology/geography/vintage effects; do not substitute Swiss 2015 data or assert high-contribution suitability.

Prepared CLIC/supplement callers are outside this native endpoint review. Other combustion, gas-supply/direct-process emissions and particulate/VOC definitions remain unfinished; public emissions support stays gated.
